text:
alex_talent: quick question — I'm starting unpaid medical leave on 2026-04-15. Will Redwood still match 401k contributions while I'm on unpaid leave, or is match only for paid payroll? Also can I make up contributions retroactively when I return? :thinking:

jenna_hr: hey @alex_talent :wave: short answer: employer match is calculated on eligible compensation we actually pay you. so if there are no payroll contributions during unpaid leave, there won't be a match for that period.

jenna_hr: on the retroactive part — we can't backdate payroll deductions for past paychecks. sometimes the plan/vendor allows an "employee catch-up" or one-time after-the-fact contribution if it meets IRS/plan rules, but it's not guaranteed. pls DM me your exact leave dates and we'll check with the vendor.

paul-payroll: adding payroll detail — cutoff for changes/contributions is EOD two business days before payroll runs. if you plan to change deferral before leave, make sure it hits payroll by that cutoff. if you're already unpaid, the only path is an off-cycle or vendor-processed contribution which needs manual approval.

alex_talent: thanks. for the loan I have through the 401k, will repayments stop? what happens if there's no paycheck to take the deduction from?

paul-payroll: loan repayments are normally payroll-deducted. if there is no payroll, you need to set up an ACH debit with the plan vendor to keep payments current. if loan payments are missed and not cured, the outstanding balance can be treated as a distribution (taxable + potential 10% early distribution if under 59½). DM me and I can initiate the vendor ACH setup.

benefits-bot: Helpful link: https://benefits.redwood.example/401k-faq (see section "Leaves of Absence and Contributions")

jenna_hr: next steps for you @alex_talent: 1) confirm exact leave start/end dates here 2) if you want to try a vendor catch-up, tell me how much you'd like to contribute (we'll verify plan rules) 3) let paul know if you need ACH set up for loan payments.

alex_talent: leave 2026-04-15 to 2026-06-14. I want to contribute extra once back if possible — willing to do whatever vendor paperwork required. also will probably need the ACH for the loan.

paul-payroll: got it. I'll open a ticket with the vendor (Forus Retirement Services) asking about one-time catch-up and ACH loan option. sample email I'll send: ```Subject: Off-cycle contribution & ACH setup for emp 12345
Employee: Alex T.
Leave: 2026-04-15 to 2026-06-14
Request: eligibility for catch-up contribution for missed payroll periods; ACH setup for loan repayment```

mike-peopleops: FWIW managers: remind folks going unpaid >30 days to check benefits & loans. small admin lift but avoids surprises. :thumbsup:

jenna_hr: thanks @mike-peopleops — we'll also add a checklist to the LOA workflow.

alex_talent: perfect, appreciate everyone. I'll DM the docs now. :thanks:
